correctness.rationale: For two selected frame rows R, the real 2×(n−2) Stiefel completion has density det(I−RᵀR)^((n−5)/2) at n≥4. Polar row coordinates have constant ds dt dα dβ Jacobian and doubling row angles correctly maps to ψ; determinant is D=1−s−t+st(1−cosψ)/2. Higher n multiplies density by D^((m−n)/2), strictly decreasing likelihood ratio in cosψ. At n=5 the full-support density is flat; sign comparisons follow angle pairing or support. For n=4 and s+t>1, x=sin²(ψ/2)∈(q,1), beta-elliptic substitution yields 1−2qE(1−1/q)/K(1−1/q). The monotone likelihood-ratio comparison in v=(x−q)/(1−q), with x increasing in both q and v, proves a unique crossing. Independently integrated four n values and the elliptic root. Excludes the null conditioning surface s+t=1.

value.rationale: Correlations of labelled edge directions conditional on lengths are a natural question in the symmetric closed-polygon ensemble. A universal pentagonal uniformity threshold and explicit elliptic crossover for quadrilaterals represent a complete, interpretable statistical classification, not a routine marginal re-expression.

final_claim: For Haar-real-Stiefel n×2 closed planar polygons (n≥4), two lengths s,t∈(0,1), s+t≠1 condition the angle ψ with density proportional to 1_{D>0}D^((n−5)/2). Mean cosine is positive/zero/negative for n=4/5/≥6 when s+t<1; if s+t>1 it is negative for n≥5 and for n=4 crosses once at q*≈0.173885234015, defined by an elliptic-integral equation.
limitations: Only symmetric Haar-real-Stiefel ensemble of perimeter two; arbitrary random polygon laws are not covered.
q*=0.173885... is numerical corroboration, while uniqueness is analytic and holds for 0<q<1.
residual_risks: General truncated-Stiefel Jacobian is classical, and a rarely indexed joint-angle calculation could imply parts of the phase diagram.
